newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shortage fears drive up Colombo rubber prices.
newsitem.headline: Shortage fears drive up Colombo rubber prices.

text.p: Crepe prices rose at the Colombo auction on Thursday because of fears of a shortage due to rain in rubber growing areas, brokers said.
"Quantities are a bit low these days because rain is hampering tapping," said a broker for John Keells. "The market is expecting a shortfall in the immediate future."
On offer were 130 tonnes of crepe and 44 tonnes of scrap, about half the quantity that is usually sold over the Colombo auction.

"Exporters are terribly short. Under pressure from overseas buyers, they are buying up whatever that is available and pushing up the market," said Lanil Waniganayake of export firm Almar Trading Company.
Best latex one-x, the purest grade, fetched 87.65 rupees ($1.50) per kg compared to 85 rupees last week. Number one fetched 86.25 from 62.15 last week, while RSS 1 went unquoted.
Rain, which immediately hampers rubber tapping, in the long-term also reduces latex quality, brokers said. ($1=58.55) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
